newsitem.title: UK: European shares shed gains as Wall Street sags.
newsitem.headline: European shares shed gains as Wall Street sags.

text.p: European bourses pared morning strength to close only modestly higher after Wall Street speedily surrendered a 75 point opening rally.
The dollar remained firm against European currencies, but key bond markets tumbled in late trade after a French opinion poll hurt sentiment.
Paris, helped earlier to a 30 point gain by the firmer dollar and strong bonds, shed most of this ground to close up a mere six points at 2,540 after the IPSOS poll for French weekly Le Point.
The poll suggested that France's centre-right government would only win a thin majority in snap elections on May 25 and June 1.
Frankfurt's after-hours Ibis DAX index held most of its strength to end 30 points higher at 3,396, but failed to hold above the key support level of 3,400 after New York slipped.

The Dow Jones industrial average opened ahead and quickly rallied 75 points to 6,890.59, bouncing back from Wednesday's 21-point sell-off in anticipation that good corporate results would lead the market higher.
But weak U.S. treasuries quickly undermined the gains and the Dow sagged.

London, transfixed by the country's general election next week, had already ignored Wall Street's open and shrugged off British inflation data easing fears of an immediate interest rate rise after the May 1 vote.
As a result, its fractional gain over the day went unchallenged and the FTSE 100 index of blue-chip stocks ended 0.80 of a point higher at 4,388.5 for an eighth consecutive rise.
March CPI, Britain's new measure of consumer price inflation, earlier showed a 1.8 percent yearly rise which strategists said would cap interest rate fears.
But traders said gains were capped in the run-up to next week's election and volume remained slim at 699 million.

"We are struggling at the 4,400 level," one dealer said. "There was a lack of follow-through buying today and things were dampened by the bond market which was very dull." The leading index earlier touched 4,400.4 before drifting back.
In the currency market dollar sentiment stood firm in late European trade after tame German inflation data trimmed expectations that interest rates there would soon rise.

However, operators were wary of pushing the dollar very far ahead of a Group of Seven finance ministers' meeting this weekend in Washington and the dollar had backed off its highs against the mark by late trade.
Talks between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, scheduled for Friday, were also keeping traders' hands tied.
STOCK CLOSING LEVELS
London's FTSE 100 closed 0.80 points up at 4,388.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index ended 6.19 higher at 2539.83.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 1.41 points at 3397.36. The IBIS DAX index was up 29.62 At 3396.49
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7150 against the mark versus 1.7117 in late European trade on Wednesday.
Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 125.95 from 126.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD fixed at $340.90, down 25 cents from the morning, trading in a narrow range in fairly quiet trade. Resistance was seen at $342.50, support at $340.00.
SILVER was steady and quiet at $4.71, down a cent.
